L1_MULTIPLICATIVITY.citation: H. Davenport, H. Heilbronn (1936), on the zeros of certain Dirichlet series, J. London Math. Soc. (papers I-II): zeta(s,a) for rational (and transcendental) a, and combinations of the Davenport-Heilbronn type, have infinitely many zeros in Re s > 1
L1_MULTIPLICATIVITY.witness: a_6 != a_2 a_3.  EXACT WITNESS (coefficients of f in K = Q(zeta_20), coordinates on 1, z, ..., z^7): a_2 = kappa = (-1, 2, 0, -1, -1, 1, 1, -1), a_3 = -kappa, a_6 = 1 (6 = 1 mod 5).  a_2 a_3 = -kappa^2 and a_6 - a_2 a_3 = 1 + kappa^2 = (6, -4, 0, 0, 2, -2, -2, 4) != 0; nonzero-ness certified by Norm_{K/Q}(1 + kappa^2) = 6400 (product over all 8 Galois conjugates, exact).  All three coefficients lie in the real quartic subfield Q(kappa).  LEMMA (formal, proved): a formal Dirichlet series with a_1 = 1 admitting ANY Euler product over the rational primes with unital local factors (local constant term 1) has multiplicative coefficients — the coefficient of n^{-s} in prod_p L_p is prod_p b_{p, v_p(n)}.  Hence a_6 != a_2 a_3 refutes every such factorization of f, for this (intrinsic) normalization; a vertical shift s -> s + c rescales both sides of a_6 = a_2 a_3 by 6^{-c} and changes nothing.  SCOPE: this refutes multiplicativity of THIS normalization (a_1 = 1, the one forced by any unital Euler product); it is a single exact triple, which is all that is needed

L2_EULER_PRODUCT.citation: H. Davenport, H. Heilbronn (1936), on the zeros of certain Dirichlet series, J. London Math. Soc. (papers I-II): zeta(s,a) for rational (and transcendental) a, and combinations of the Davenport-Heilbronn type, have infinitely many zeros in Re s > 1
